spots.name: El-Jazzar Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The el-Jazzar Mosque, also known as the White Mosque of Acre, is located on el-Jazzar Street inside the walls of the old city of Acre, Israel, overlooking the eastern Mediterranean Sea, and is named after the Ottoman Bosnian governor Ahmad Pasha el-Jazzar.

spots.name: Shrine of Baháʼu'lláh

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Shrine of Baháʼu'lláh, known among Baháʼís as the Blessed Shrine, is the burial place of Baháʼu'lláh, the founder of the Baháʼí Faith. It stands at Bahjí, just north of Acre in northern Israel.

spots.name: Old City of Acre
spots.summary: The Old City of Acre is the historical center of Acre, in northern Israel. Known for its cultural, architectural, and social heritage, the Old City is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is an ancient port city, with a history dating back to the Bronze Age.

spots.name: Hospitaller commandery of Saint-Jean-d'Acre

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Hospitaller commandery of Saint-Jean-d'Acre is a monumental complex founded by the Order of St. John of Jerusalem, also known as the Knights Hospitallers. It is located in the city of Saint-Jean-d'Acre. In the 13th century, the commandery became the headquarters of the Order until the fall of the city in 1291.

spots.name: Cathedral of the Holy Cross, Acre

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of the Holy Cross was the main Latin cathedral of the Diocese of Acre in the Kingdom of Jerusalem. It stood in the medieval city of Acre until the fall of the Crusader presence in 1291. In 1781, the El-Jazzar Mosque was constructed on or near the site traditionally identified with the former cathedral.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of the Holy Cross, Acre

spots.summary: The Ghetto Fighters' House is a Holocaust museum founded in 1949 by members of Kibbutz Lohamei Hagetaot. It is located in the Western Galilee, Israel, on the Coastal Highway between Acre (Akko) and Nahariya.

spots.summary: Khan al-Umdan is the largest and best preserved caravanserai in Acre, Israel. Located in the Old City of Acre, it is one of the prominent projects constructed during the rule of Ahmed Jezzar Pasha in Galilee, under the Ottoman era.

spots.summary: The al-Muallak Mosque also known as the Mosque of Daher al-Umar is a mosque, located in Acre, in the northern district of Israel.

spots.name: Church of St John the Baptist

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St John the Baptist was the principal church of the Knights Hospitaller in the Crusader city of Acre. It stood within the Hospitaller commandery of Saint-Jean-d'Acre, forming part of the complex now beneath the Ottoman Citadel of Acre.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of St John the Baptist (Hospitaller, Acre)

spots.name: Church of Saint Andrew, Acre

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Andrew's Church is a Melkite Greek Catholic church. Built in 1765, it is located in the old city of Acre, at Philippe Auguste street, north of the Templars tunnel in modern-day Israel. It is named after one of the twelve apostles of Jesus. The church was built on the remains of a Crusader church.

spots.name: St. John Baptist Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The St. John Baptist Church sometimes simply called Church of St. John, is a Catholic church located in the town of Acre in northern Israel.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Saint John the Baptist Church, Acre

spots.name: Akko Light
spots.summary: Akko Light or Acre Light, is an active lighthouse in the port of Acre, Israel. It is located on the South-West corner of the city's ancient walls, at what is believed to be the former site of an Ottoman Burj-El-Sanjak.

spots.name: St. George church, Acre

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint George Greek Orthodox Cathedral is an Orthodox church and monastery located in Acre, Israel. It dates back to 16th century and is built on the ruins of a Byzantine church. The walls of the church were covered with carved wood.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Saint George Greek Orthodox Cathedral, Acre

spots.summary: The Treasures in the Walls Museum is an ethnographic museum located in Acre, Israel. The museum is dedicated to show the craftsmanship of the city of Acre.

spots.summary: The Terra Sancta Church, also alternatively Church of St. Francis, is the name given to one of the two Franciscan-run Roman Catholic churches located in the Old City of Acre in northern Israel, the other one being the Church of St. John the Baptist.

spots.name: Acre Municipal Stadium
spots.summary: Acre Municipal Stadium, also Toto Acre Stadium, is a soccer stadium in Acre, Israel. It is the home ground of Hapoel Acre which plays in Liga Leumit, the second tier of the Israeli football league system. The stadium is located at the southern entrance of town, near the Ein HaMifratz intersection.
